mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect inverts during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a supply chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a broader economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a compositional shift toward lower-wage employment, which reduces average labor productivity and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of rapid wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average by more than 5% signals increased household dissaving and higher consumption financed by debt, which temporarily supports corporate revenues but ultimately raises default risk and inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong income growth.
